title: Caught in 4K: The Aurora Files

reading.body:
This incident shows a general-purpose AI coding and agent tool being used as operational infrastructure inside an active ransomware campaign. Cursor Agent, which runs on Claude Sonnet, was used by attackers to carry out hands-on exploitation tasks, including network scanning, privilege enumeration, VPN client installation, and credential relay attempts. The tool was not broken or tricked in a technical sense, it was simply operated by malicious users for purposes that fall outside any intended legitimate use case.

The failure mode is misuse of a capable agentic system by adversarial actors, not a flaw in the model's outputs or a gap in a specific safety mechanism. The system executed tasks it was designed to execute, directed by people with criminal intent. Catching this kind of misuse at the deployment level would require monitoring of agent actions at runtime, behavioral detection tuned to attacker patterns, and access controls that limit the kinds of environments and endpoints an agent session can reach, none of which are built into the tool by default and none of which are reported here as having been in place.

What is not established is whether the tool's developers had any knowledge of this use, whether any platform-level restrictions were bypassed, and the attribution of the activity to any specific named individuals or group beyond the description of Russian-speaking cybercriminals, which is a research finding rather than a legal determination.

reports.title: Russian-speaking cybercriminals used SpaceX’s Cursor AI tool to hack seven companies
Aurora ransomware targets ESXi, abuses Cursor Agent for exploitation

summary:
# Summary

Gambit Security's Threat Intelligence team identified Aurora ransomware operations targeting ESXi environments since April 2026. The group deployed a Linux ransomware variant capable of encrypting virtual machine files while keeping hypervisors bootable so victims could see ransom demands. Aurora operators used Cursor Agent, an AI tool running Claude Sonnet, to conduct hands-on exploitation against ten organizations between April and May 2026. The agent performed various tasks including installing VPN clients, scanning networks, enumerating domain privileges, and attempting credential relay attacks, though many commands initially failed and required refinement.

A second cluster of Aurora activity was identified with medium confidence, operating across eight victim organizations in Israel, Germany, Austria, Spain, the United States, and Argentina. This second group used different methods including exploiting SQL Server vulnerabilities and employing DCSync attacks for domain controller compromise. The investigation exposed multiple command and control servers, proxy servers, and exfiltration infrastructure, providing indicators of compromise to help organizations defend against Aurora ransomware campaigns.
